# Constant-argument temporal operators

Generated by `dive-conformance dev capture` against `tlc-2026.10.06.014338`,
using the bundled modules and JRE, `-workers 1 -lncheck final -seed 0 -fp 0`.
Clean transcripts supply verdicts/counts. Violation traces come from a separate
cross-checked trace pass; `.command` files preserve the exact invocation.

```sh
DIVE_CACHE_DIR=<verified-cache> cargo run -p dive-conformance --release -- dev capture \
  --oracle tlc-2026.10.06.014338 \
  --specs crates/dive-api/tests/fixtures/temporal-calls/specs \
  --out crates/dive-api/tests/fixtures/temporal-calls \
  PcVisit PcFair PcStable PcScopes PcTuple
```

Each probe explores 5 generated / 2 distinct states, depth 2.
`PcVisit` and fair `PcStable` violate P (exit 13); fair `PcFair`/`PcScopes`
and `PcTuple` succeed. The probes exercise constant scalar/tuple arguments,
quantified call sites, nested calls and repeated bodies under different values.

Tests compare final truth/counts in both profiles and stores and independently
validate every returned periodic claim. Direct short-word controls enumerate
all boolean words of lengths 1–4 and closing targets. State-dependent arguments,
checker-register reads hidden in arguments and effectful calls remain refusals.
TLC-exact planning/selection, phase-L timing and broader lazy/higher-order calls
remain pending; this is supported-subset evidence, not strict liveness conformance.
